title: Which Pair? · Teams
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Which Pair? · Teams with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: The lead writes four familiar objects, with exactly two that share an agreed visible property. The lead reads the list and names the property without identifying the pair. The others identify the two objects that share the property. Form two teams. Each team has four turns; only the lead’s teammates respond or assist. Each success earns the team one point. The higher team score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Which Pair?, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The others identify the two objects that share the property.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The others identify the two objects that share the property.
